recentItems.title: China to Build, Upgrade 7,400 km of "Golden Outer Ring" Highway Loop by 2030
recentItems.description:
China plans to invest more than 55 billion U.S. dollars for upgrades and construction to parts of its "Golden Outer Ring" highway that, when finished, will be a massive roadway that runs along the country’s entire perimeter.

According to the Ministry of Transport, China plans to build or upgrade about 7,400 kilometers of the highway during the current 15th Five-Year Plan that ends in 2030.

Part of the upgrades include the completion of the Donggang Grand Bridge, a key project for National Highway G228, one of the three national highways that comprise the Golden Outer Ring.

Meanwhile, the section of national highway G331 from the Tongjiang-Suibin Border to Suibin in northeast China is undergoing a reconstruction and expansion project.

The highway is comprised of the G228, the G331 and the G219 National Highways.

When finished, the Golden Outer Ring will be about 27,000 kilometers long.

recentItems.title: China's AI Surge Sparks Wave of Compute Infrastructure Buildouts
recentItems.description:
In China, an ongoing AI revolution is spawning a wave of new token factories and intelligent computing centers, built to feed the country's voracious hunger for compute.

One of the latest additions is this Beijing token mill, which only went live in June and is already churning out the tiny data units that feed AI models, at scale.

Elsewhere in the country, intelligent computing centers are also springing up in cities like Guangzhou, with domestically produced chips, hardware, and architecture becoming increasingly prevalent.

Data shows that by the end of last year, China's intelligent computing capacity reached 1.59 million PFLOPS – or roughly 1,590 quintillion floating-point operations per second.
